name: Title 3
text:
EEG AI Honours
Project Kickoff

name: Subtitle 4
text: A project for one student, with room for a team

name: Rounded Rectangle 2
text: 26 October 2026

Audience: an introductory computer science honours student and potential supervisor/team. This proposal replaces the earlier PhD-programme framing. The project is successful when the student can reproduce, explain and evaluate a controlled study. A transformer improvement is a hypothesis, not a promised deliverable. No new experiments were run for this kickoff.

text: Project kickoff

name: Google Shape;533;p58
text: The core project

name: Google Shape;534;p58
text:
A question we can answer
Can EEG features predict reported sleep experience in unseen participants? Compare a simple spectral classifier with a tiny transformer.

name: Google Shape;534;p58
text:
A result we can demonstrate
Build an EEG model-comparison viewer. Show the features, report labels, predictions and failure cases. Keep EEG-to-BOLD as a separate extension.

text:
DREAM EEG and report labels
Audit people, cases and sleep stages

text:
Fixed pre-awakening history
Spectral features in time bins

name: diagram-models
text:
Logistic baseline / tiny transformer
One optional pooling change

name: diagram-evaluation
text:
Held-out people
Stage controls, scores and demo

Recommended starter: the public Zhang and Wamsley 2019 subset in the Monash-associated DREAM collection. Labels are participant reports (0=no experience, 2=experience), not dream content or a definitive test of consciousness. First audit sleep-stage availability and label balance within stages. The diagram describes a proposed offline classification study, not a completed model or clinical device. If BOLD prediction is essential, the existing ds006040 compact feature cache is a faster continuity alternative, subject to reuse checks. Sources: https://figshare.com/articles/dataset/Zhang_Wamsley_2019_Final/22226692 ; https://api.figshare.com/v2/articles/22226692 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12350935/ .

text: One question, three concrete deliverables

name: Google Shape;534;p58
text:
A reproducible baseline
Audit one EEG subset. Fit a spectral logistic classifier with participant-grouped splits. Include majority and sleep-stage controls.

name: Content Placeholder 1
text:
An explanatory demo
Show signals, scores and failures. Include a short report and a walkthrough the student can give without relying on AI-written explanations.

name: Content Placeholder 2
text:
One transformer study
After the baseline works, compare mean pooling with learned time-bin weighting. Keep the same features and split. A clear negative result counts.

name: Content Placeholder 15
text: DEMO

The proposed pooling change is a bounded teaching experiment, not a claimed novel architecture or physiological explanation. Use identical window features, a tiny encoder and a shared evaluation. It is optional until ingestion, label balance and the baseline work. Include a stage-only control or a stage-matched analysis where the labels support it. If categories do not vary within stage/participant sufficiently, report the confounding limit rather than interpreting classification as an experience-specific marker. Original analysis to reproduce in part: https://zenodo.org/records/15234846 .

name: Title 2
text: Monash resources worth using

name: Content Placeholder 9
text:
M3 and eResearch
Reuse the working cluster connection. Confirm CI-led project access and limits. Use CPU baselines, a GPU pilot and HPC training or drop-ins.

name: Content Placeholder 10
text:
DREAM and Turner
Start with a public DREAM subset. Seek a sleep/EEG adviser through a supervisor. A Monash-hosted collection is not automatically Monash-collected data.

name: Content Placeholder 9
text:
Biomedical Imaging
MBI lists EEG and simultaneous EEG-fMRI support. Treat new recordings as optional, with facility training, ethics, bookings and a budget.

name: Content Placeholder 10
text:
IT and DeepNeuron
The IT EEG representation-learning project is a supervision lead. DeepNeuron offers a possible AI/HPC student community. Places and collaboration need confirmation.

Checked 26 October 2026. A read-only M3 squeue check succeeded and showed no current jobs for this account; this is not a new student's entitlement or unrestricted allocation. No jobs were submitted. M3 is not certified for sensitive data; establish classification and an approved platform before a controlled clinical extension. MAVERIC is a conditional specialised route, not required for the starter. Some MBI details were available only in indexed official text, not a live booking check. Sources: https://docs.erc.monash.edu/Compute/HPC/M3/ ; https://docs.erc.monash.edu/Compute/HPC/M3/GettingStarted/CreateM3Project/ ; https://docs.erc.monash.edu/Compute/HPC/M3/TermsOfUse/ ; https://docs.erc.monash.edu/Training/DropInSessions/ ; https://www.monash.edu/researchinfrastructure/mbi/facilities/human/eeg ; https://www.monash.edu/researchinfrastructure/mbi/forms-and-policies ; https://www.supervisorconnect.it.monash.edu/index.php/projects/research/learning-massive-amounts-eeg-data .

name: TextBox 11
text:
Zhang and Wamsley subset: 28 participants and 308 catalogued cases, under CC BY 4.0. The collection is Monash-associated; this cohort was collected at Furman University.
Audit usable cases and sleep-stage confounding before training.

name: Content Placeholder 10
text:
Fallback: Sleep-EDF
Use one EEG derivation and scored sleep stages. Keep both nights from each person in the same partition.

name: Content Placeholder 10
text:
Extension: ds006040
Reuse the paired EEG-fMRI pipeline if needed. It released 28 people; our earlier analysis retained 27.

DREAM counts are catalogue counts, not a completed raw-recording QC audit. The selected public package separately declares CC BY 4.0. Other DREAM packages can have different access conditions. EEG-only recordings have no measured BOLD target. Sleep-EDF has 197 recordings overall, not 197 people; the cassette cohort has 78 participant IDs across 153 recordings. ds006040 snapshot 1.0.2 is CC0. Sources: https://figshare.com/articles/dataset/Zhang_Wamsley_2019_Final/22226692 ; https://api.figshare.com/v2/articles/22226692 ; https://bridges.monash.edu/articles/dataset/The_DREAM_database/22133105/9 ; https://physionet.org/content/sleep-edfx/1.0.0/sleep-cassette/ ; https://mne.tools/stable/auto_tutorials/clinical/60_sleep.html ; https://openneuro.org/datasets/ds006040/versions/1.0.2 . Existing ds006040/VU tests were already explored; reusing them is an educational development benchmark, not fresh confirmation.

name: Google Shape;534;p58
text: One student owns the complete small pipeline. A team of three or four can divide these roles once the baseline works. Each person should explain the shared experiment and identify their own contribution.

Suggested integration contract: dataset_id, participant_id, run_id, time_s, fold, split, target_name, y_true, y_pred, model_id and seed in the prediction table. Use immutable split/config manifests, shared metric code and small synthetic fixtures. Never infer independent sample size from overlapping windows. The optional team size is a planning suggestion, not an approved Monash programme.

name: Title 2
text: A controlled study with a fixed budget

name: Content Placeholder 9
text: Logistic classifier, tiny transformer and pooling variant.

name: Content Placeholder 10
text: Proposed GPU-hour ceiling for the initial study. Review after one pilot fit.

name: Content Placeholder 11
text: One pooling change after the baseline and data checks work.

name: Content Placeholder 15
text:
Proposed starting limits
Begin with CPU baselines and fewer than 20,000 transformer parameters. Include majority and sleep-stage controls. Select on validation; report balanced accuracy, macro F1 and uncertainty over people. Freeze a budget before evaluation. These are teaching choices.

Three study configurations plus majority and stage-only controls. The 24 GPU-hour cap is a proposed ceiling, not an entitlement or runtime estimate. Profile one validation-only fit before setting the actual cap. A possible tiny encoder has width 32, one layer, two heads and channel-averaged band features per time bin; confirm window duration from the recordings, then record the true parameter count. Compare mean pooling with learned time-bin weighting while keeping the encoder and inputs fixed. The subset is small, so overfitting is plausible and a transformer loss is informative. Evaluate with participant-grouped folds; define label support and undefined metrics, keep model selection in inner validation, and bootstrap people rather than windows. A new split does not erase any earlier test exposure. Attention or pooling weights do not prove mechanism. EEG-only metrics differ from the optional BOLD route, which requires r, raw predictive R2, error in target units and person-level comparisons.

The calendar is illustrative, not booked meetings or a claim that the full pipeline fits into four weeks. Teach-back questions: what is the report label, what is a participant/window, what does spectral power measure, how does regularisation work, how do attention and pooling differ, why might sleep stage explain the result, and which data choose settings? For BOLD extensions add haemodynamic timing and r versus predictive R2. AI can draft code, checks and captions. The student should trace a score to its source rows, make a small unaided code change and explain failures. Document AI assistance and follow the unit's actual assessment policy.

name: Rounded Rectangle 2
text: Honours project proposal

First decisions: confirm supervisor and official course requirements; choose DREAM starter or existing paired-cache continuity route; confirm data reuse/ethics route and compute limits; agree the baseline/demo deliverables; identify a domain adviser and whether extra students add useful capacity. Candidate student applications are a sleep-EEG model-comparison viewer or a research BOLD-prediction replay. Report-label classification does not decode dreams. Independent endpoints and clinical validation would be needed for patient-facing use. Keep new recording and patient-data projects optional. Read the source-linked opportunity brief and the reusable AI working prompt in reports/honours_kickoff/.
